title: Guidance API entry
description: Schema for one guidance-api/<id>.json file. See guidance-api/README.md for the full rationale (why this is a separate API from component-api), this file is the machine-checkable version of that same schema.

id.description: Must match the id used for the same component in component-api exactly, this is the join key. Not a tag name: some entries (like toolbox) have no real custom element behind them at all.

dos.description: Things to do. May be empty. Not padded to hit a count, if only one real thing is worth saying, there's one entry.

donts.description: Things to avoid, ideally naming the concrete symptom of getting it wrong, not just "don't do X".

behavior.description: Optional. Neutral facts about how the component actually behaves at runtime (what triggers a state change, what real element or event backs an interaction, what condition picks between two real implementations). Often the single most load-bearing fact about the component, sometimes already stated quietly in an attribute or event's own description elsewhere in component-api, surfaced here in one obvious place the same way dos/donts already restate a real fact for emphasis. Not advice: a dos/donts entry says what to do about a fact, a behavior entry just states the fact. May be absent entirely; most entries won't have one yet.

layout.description: Optional. Static facts about which props/attributes/slots are only meaningful together, mutually exclusive, or gate one another, a discriminated union in the component's own API surface, Nathan Curtis's "layout and configurations". Different axis from behavior: behavior is about WHEN something happens at runtime, layout is about which combination of props is even valid or renders differently in the first place (card.expanded only means anything when type="accordion"; a component's supportPage attribute and its support-link slot are mutually gated). Not a restatement of token-api's own spacing/sizing values, this is about the component's API shape, not its visual spacing. May be absent entirely; most entries won't have one yet.

a11y.description: Optional. Real accessibility facts verified against Firefox's own source: a real ARIA role or attribute the component sets, a real keyboard interaction model it implements, a real focus-management behavior. Same bar as every other field here, someone read the actual implementation and wrote down what's really there; not general accessibility best practice, a confirmed fact about this component's own code. May be absent entirely; most entries won't have one yet.

text.description: One sentence, citing something concrete and specific to this component's real implementation (a method, property, or lifecycle behavior), not generic UX advice.
